title.narrative: Health & Education ME& Capacity Building IDF Grant

description.narrative: Description of the IDF-financed components and activities 1. Capacity building in designing and implementing survey instruments for assessing outcomes. a) Training workshops in results-oriented M&Ecomma b) Technical assistance in questionnaire development and sampling designcomma and c) Implementation of pilot surveys (perhaps through the design and piloting of a single cross-sectoral survey instrument that captures the linkages between health and schooling of children etc). 2. Strengthening analytical capacity and links with policy making a) Training in data analysiscomma b) Workshops for integration of results in sectoral strategies. 3. Improve access to datacomma and dissemination of results a) Website - access to primary datacomma b) Workshopscomma c) Publication in national language. Likely outcomes of IDF-financed activities 1. Strengthened in-house capacity to produce and implement adequate instruments to measure outcomes. 2. Implementation of results-oriented M&E systems in health and education. 3. Increased capacity of using and analyzing survey data in addition to administrative data to assess policy options. 4. Increased production of analyses and reports by national researchers as a result of increased access to primary data. TF057380 Assist the Government to develop and implement outcomes-oriented M&E approaches in the health and education sectors. We propose to focus on M&E capacity building in these two sectors because (i) the Bank's short and medium term dialogue in Uzbekistan is likely to focus on health and education sectorscomma as we describe in the next section; (ii) there is no tradition of impact-analysis in Uzbekistan and there are payoffs to being selective at this stage; (iii) education and health sectors present similar M&E challenges: for example there is a time-lag between interventions (saycomma provision of learning materials or flour fortification) and observed outcomes (improvements in students# learning and reductions in the prevalence of anemia) in both sectors; and (iv) there are strong linkages between health and education (the Bank's regional household survey data reveal that sickness is the number one reason for non-attendance in basic and secondary education schoolscomma followed by agricultural work). Improve access of user groups to primary datacomma ensure sufficient dissemination of results. Access to primary data is limited in Uzbekistancomma especially when it comes to the surveys that are implemented by the Government agencies (for example the Household Budget Survey data). There has been some progress in recent years though: for examplecomma the 2002 Health Examination Survey data are available to public. The broader goal here is to contribute to enhanced transparency in public policy making by increasing the access to and utilization of other data sets (including the three wave regional LSMS household survey that the Bank's poverty team conducted; as well as the data that will be collected as part of the IDF activities).
